text:
It's holding up nicely out there right now, 82 and partly cloudy with that light west breeze, but the sky's going to start earning its keep this afternoon. Mostly sunny still gets you to a high near 86, and most of Burlington proper likely stays dry. The pop-up storms today favor the higher terrain out toward the Adirondacks, drifting our way only sometimes, so it's a hit-or-miss setup after 5pm rather than a washout. If you do get hit, it could come as a heavy downpour for a few minutes, then it's back to sun. The models don't love each other today either, the American keeps things mostly dry while the European is soggier, so I'd keep the rain jacket within reach even under blue sky.

The lake's calm and pleasant for now, water at 74 and waves a foot or less, but wind builds to 15-20 knots overnight as a south flow kicks in, so wrap up any evening paddle or sail by full dark. The bigger story is tomorrow and Wednesday, when a slow-moving system brings more widespread, potentially heavy rain and a real risk of localized flooding, not just an isolated pop-up like today.
